articleTitle: Investigation of Photobleaching Dynamics of Functionalized Curcumin in PVC for Antimicrobial Photodynamic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study investigates the photobleaching behavior of curcumin-functionalized endotracheal tubes (ETTs) under a specific laser exposure of 455nm of emission. The UV-vis absorption spectra showed a significant reduction in absorbance, indicating the degradation of curcumin. Fluorescence of the ETT surface demonstrate the decrease in the curcumin depending on the exposure dose and DMSO-extracted solutions displayed altered fluorescence and the emergence of new chromatographic bands, with species having m/z values of 296, 385, 415, and 427, which were not present in the original curcumin solution. These findings suggest the formation of unknown photoproducts during the photobleaching process. Understanding these degradation pathways is essential for optimizing the performance of curcumin-functionalized materials in photodynamic applications.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Distributed Macrobending Loss in Optical Fiber Path Using Differential Geometry
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Optical fiber macrobend loss is considered a problem regarding applications in telecommunications. On the other hand, macrobending losses are exploited in the design of macrobend loss based sensors. This work presents a mathematical modeling based on differential geometry to compute the total macrobending loss of an optical fiber path. To experimentally demonstrate the model, a Corning smf-28e+ optical fiber was experimentally characterized for bend loss. Then predictions of the bend loss for a deformed fiber coil were performed and experimentally validated.

articleTitle: A Radio- and Power-Over-Fiber System Using Double-Clad Fiber Towards B5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This paper presents the integration of radio- and power-over-fiber (RPoF) for beyond-fifth-generation (B5G) systems using double-clad fibers (DCFs) to deliver data and power simultaneously. We propose a system that transmits a 5G new radio (NR) signal centered at 26 GHz and over 20- W optical power through a 250-m DCF link. In this setup, the PoF system is able to power critical components of the RoF system, including a photodetector (PD) and electrical amplifier (EA). Our experimental performance investigation is based on power efficiency and stability analysis, as well as root mean square error vector magnitude <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{EVM}_{\text{RMS}})$</tex> measurements. The results demonstrate that the proposed RPoF system meets the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\text{rd}}$</tex> Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) requirements without degradation from the high-power feed light. Additionally, a throughput of 1.6 Gbps is achieved, demonstrating the feasibility of using DCFs in RPoF systems.

articleTitle: Delayed Luminescence Tests with Algae Under Zinc Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The stress of algae samples due exposure to Zinc is expressed in their delayed luminescence patterns, whose alterations in decay dynamics can be related to the solution's toxicity. Indicative results are obtained just one hour after inoculation, with sensitivity comparable to those of standard tests (in 72h) but using less consumables/work-hours. Further tests using different metals might validate the new data analysis suggested in the article.

articleTitle: Random Convolutional Kernel Transformation and Regression Models for Chlorophyll Estimation in Leaves from Reflection Spectra
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study compares traditional and advanced machine learning methods, such as MiniRocket and Deep Neural Networks, for non-destructive estimation of chlorophyll content in plant leaves using reflection spectroscopy within the 400–800 nm spectral range. The results show that MiniRocket offers the highest accuracy, with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> of 0.982 (test data), highlighting its effectiveness in providing accurate chlorophyll predictions.

articleTitle: Combined Effects of Optical Therapy and Stem Cells for Tendon Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Tendon injuries often fail to fully regenerate after surgery, leading to impaired function and possible graft rejection. Advances in regenerative medicine include tendon engineering with stem cells. Herein, we demonstrate that adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells respond differently to culture media, and red LED enhances metabolism and collagen synthesis.

articleTitle: Enhancing Passive Optical Networks Using Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers for Expanded Coverage and Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The experimental characterization of semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOA) as an alternative to enhance the performance of passive optical networks (PON) is presented. By integrating SOAs on the network topology, one can significantly improve signal quality, increase user capacity, and expand network coverage. This study highlights the potential of SOAs to transform optical network infrastructure, meeting the growing market demand.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Influence of Different Illuminants on Skin Color Classification Using the Individual Typology Angle
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of different illuminants on the classification of skin tones using the Individual Typology Angle (ITA). The analysis was conducted through numerical simulations that considered skin colors under the standard D65 illuminant and four other illuminants (FL2, LED-V2, LED-B1, and HP1). First, skin colors were converted to the CIELAB color space, and then ITA values were calculated to classify the colors into specific categories. Additionally, perceptible differences in skin colors were measured using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta E_{2000}$</tex> color difference metric. The results showed that changes in lighting significantly affect the perception of skin colors, with a tendency for a shift in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b^{*}$</tex> axis of the CIELAB color space, indicating an increase in the intensity of yellow in the simulated skin samples. The FL2, LED-V2, LED-B1, and HP1 light sources showed a higher proportion of skin colors classified as brown and tan, with a reduction in the very light and light categories. These findings highlight the importance of considering the type of lighting when evaluating skin color, especially in fields such as medicine and cosmetics, where accuracy in color perception is essential.

articleTitle: Innovative Vertical Coupling Photonic Packaging Using Additive Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Coupling light to and from optical fibers is a challenge for silicon photonic due to size differences and mechanical complexity. This paper addresses the development of packaging for vertical (off-plane) coupling using 3D printing. We demonstrated that additive technology can be used to manufacture fiber arrays and vertical coupling packaging platforms, simplifying photonic packaging and enabling rapid and cost-effective customization and prototyping. Results of 250 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> resin fiber arrays are presented, describing the groove fabrication, fiber array assembly and their dimensional/optical characterization. Silicon photonic IC packaging is also shown, and evolution of these developments is mentioned.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Tunable All-Fiber Mach-Zehnder Interferometers in Hollow Core Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We demonstrate a new acousto-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZ) based on a hollow core fiber (HCF). The fabricated acousto-optic device excites two MZs in a 7.5 cm long HCF. In the first MZ, the HCF is attached in a centrally positioned acoustic driver, exciting two acoustically induced long period gratings. The second MZ induces two strong curvatures at the edges of the attached HCF-driver length. The MZs tune the free spectral range of the modulated multiwavelength spectrum by changing the driver's frequency in steps of 1 Hz while providing compactness, efficiency, and high sensitivity, suitable for dynamic filters and fiber sensors.

articleTitle: Optical System for Real-Time Monitoring of the Free Water Content Present in Diesel
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Petroleum-based products and byproducts like diesel can incorporate water during production, transportation, and storage processes. The presence of water in these products has always been a problem for the industry, causing severe damage to the equipment where they will be used and con-tributing to corrosion in storage tanks. This work addresses the development of a real-time monitoring and analysis methodology that will compose an engineering solution capable of identifying the presence of free water in storage tanks, enabling intelligent and autonomous disposal. For this purpose, an experimental plant was built that simulates the diesel/biodiesel storage process, composed of (i) storage tank, (ii) discharge tank, (iii) cleaning tank, (iv) an instrumented optical unit operating in the near-infrared and ultraviolet range, capable of reading images, (v) electromechanical devices for controlling and actuating the oper-ating modes of the developed plant, and (vi) an expert program for controlling, acquiring, and analyzing data. The optical unit is capable of analyzing and classifying in real-time the fluid present in storage tanks by near-infrared spectroscopy and UV spectrofluorimetry, as well as using computer vision techniques for fluid analysis through image recognition.

articleTitle: Analysis 1T' - MoTe2 Saturable Absorber Integrated to a Silicon Nitride Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the saturable absorption behavior of a 1T' <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\text{MoTe}_{2}$</tex> monolayer placed on top of a silicon nitride waveguide. Saturable absorption is modeled by calculating the quasi-Fermi level separation upon light absorption and carrier generation. After simulating the coupling between the monolayer and a silicon nitride waveguide, we propose an integrated saturable absorber with 20 % coupling efficiency and about 2 µW of saturation intensity, for a typical monolayer of 50 µm. Our results demonstrate significant potential for IT'- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MoTe}_{2}$</tex> in on-chip photonic devices, offering a compact and efficient alternative to conventional absorbers.

articleTitle: Bright Asynchronous Heralded Single-Photon Source Using a-Si:H Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate an on-chip pair generation rate of up to 3.1 MHz by a spontaneous four-wave mixing process in a hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) waveguide using a continuous-wave (CW) laser. By performing a heralded autocorrelation measurement, we show that even for high levels of pair generation, the source keeps emitting light in the single-photon regime.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Influence of Titanium Dioxide Nanoparticle Size on Sunscreen UV Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Sunscreens are employed to protect against the harmful effects of ultraviolet (UV) radiation, with titanium dioxide (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) nanoparticles (NPs) being one of the widely used components in sunscreen formulations. This study aims to assess, through computational simulations, the efficacy of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NPs of varying sizes and density as UV filters in sunscreens. As a result, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>demonstrated excellent UV absorption capacity, essential for sunscreens, and minimal visible backscattering, which reduces the opaque effect on the skin. It was found that NPs with diameters between 60 nm and 100 nm provide the highest sun protection factor (SPF) indices, with 100 nm being the most favorable due to reduced skin absorption. Additionally, solar filter based on TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NPs with concentrations up to 5% provides adequate SPF values for UV protection. This study helps identify the best conditions for the use of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NPs in sunscreens.

articleTitle: Antiresonant Polymer Optical Fibers for Strain Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The present work investigates the use of polymethyl-methacrylate capillaries for strain sensing based on to their antiresonance guiding mechanism. Initially, we fabricated capillary fiber sensors and analysed their quality by evaluating the thickness variation along their axis. In sequence, we experimentally evaluated the capillary transmission spectra and compared it with the theoretical predictions on the spectra positions of the transmission minima. Finally, considering the thickness and refractive index variations due to the application of strain, we simulated the shifting of the spectrum and obtained a high sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.7nm/m\epsilon$</tex> for the 1419. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6nm$</tex> valley displacement.

articleTitle: Red LED Radiation as a Potential Radioprotector Using a Zebrafish Embryo Model
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Radiation therapy (RT) is crucial for cancer treatment but often causes severe side effects that impact quality of life, emphasizing the need for better tissue radioprotection strategies. This study investigated the radioprotective potential of red LED irradiation using zebrafish embryos. After determining the median lethal dose of gamma radiation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{LD}_{\mathbf{50}})$</tex> to be 16.7 Gy, embryos were exposed to red LED before gamma radiation. While red LED alone did not affect survival rates, pre-treatment with red light increased survival to over 50% after LD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> gamma radiation. These results suggest that red LED could help reduce the acute effects of RT.

articleTitle: Characterization of Protoporphyrin IX in Experiments with Mitochondria Isolated from Mouse Liver
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) is an intermediate in heme biosynthesis, synthesized within the mitochondria. As a photosensitizer in photodynamic therapy (PDT), PpIX primarily targets mitochondrial structures. This study investigates the interaction of PpIX with mitochondria isolated from mouse liver. Absorbance analysis reveals that exogenous PpIX added to mitochondrial samples in vitro binds significantly to the mitochondria. Fluorescence analysis of mitochondria isolated after <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta-\text{aminolevulinic}$</tex> acid (ALA) injection on mice demonstrates that PpIX accumulates within the mitochondria. This is a preliminary study for subsequent in vitro experiments, where PDT will be applied to mitochondria isolated from mouse liver, focusing on analyzing mitochondrial respiration.

articleTitle: Design of a Temperature Sensor Based on Partially Filled Hollow-Core Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We report on the design of a temperature sensor based on a hollow-core optical fiber partially filled with liquid. Our findings demonstrate that partially filling the fiber hollow core with liquids results in a temperature sensor with improved resolution compared to a fully filled fiber. The sensing platform operates based on the thermo-optic effect, and the resolution enhancement is achieved by assessing the combined transmission characteristics of the hollow and liquid-filled fiber sections. We understand that our investigation indicates a promising path for developing new hollow-core fiber-based temperature sensors with better resolution levels.

articleTitle: Low-Crosstalk in 2D Waveguide Crossings by Metaheuristic Optimization Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This work describes the investigation of planar waveguide crossings using metaheuristic methods associated with the two-dimensional finite element method (2D-FEM). An optimization and measurement process are performed on the power transmission and crosstalk of the waveguide crossings and then the values calculated are compared with other studies in the literature. The best performing adjusted crossing is optimally designed by applying the following metaheuristics: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and a hybrid algorithm combining the Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure and Simulated Annealing (GRASP-SA). Transmission efficiency results higher than 97% and crosstalk below the -50 dB over a wide wavelength range, with a footprint of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4.9}\times \mathbf{4.9}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Determination of the Attenuation Coefficient by OCT in Cutaneous Melanoma After the Application of Optical Clearing Agents
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Melanoma is the most aggressive skin cancer, originating from melanin-producing melanocytes, it is highly metastatic and challenging to treat. Light-based therapies such as photodynamic and photothermal treatments are promising but limited by melanin's light-absorbing properties. Optical clearing agents (OCAs), which promotes refractive index matching, can enhance these therapies by improving light penetration. In the present study, we analyzed the effect of OCAs in a cutaneous melanoma model by obtaining the attenuation coefficient using optical coherence tomography. A reduction of up to 43% in the attenuation coefficient was observed in melanoma after OCA application, confirming their effectiveness in decreasing light attenuation, allowing deeper light penetration into the tumor.

articleTitle: Issues for Using All-Optical Wavelength Converters and Route Segmentation in Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this paper, we present and numerically evaluate some issues on the performance of optical networks using route segmentation (RS) combined with all-optical wavelength converters (AOWCs). By considering modulation formats, fiber augmentation, and wavelength conversion, the study explores the impact of RS and AOWCs on network metrics, such as blocking rate (BR) and throughput. Simulations were conducted on the CORONET topology, analyzing various bandwidth parameter values for AOWCs. Results demonstrate that RS effectively reduces BR and enhances throughput, while AOWCs also improve performance. However, these two strategies must be balanced to match cost and performance requirements.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Pure Anatase Phase $\text{TiO}_{2}$ Films Without Direct Thermal Control Applied to the Fabrication of Optical Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study develops a novel multi-step sputtering process to fabricate 150 nm thick <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> films in the pure anatase phase, overcoming challenges related to uncontrolled phase transitions during prolonged plasma exposure. By introducing a three-stage deposition approach with intervals, we achieve consistent phase purity and reproducibility. Raman spectroscopy and optical ellipsometry confirm the effectiveness of this method. The multi-step sputtering process is applied to the fabrication of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TiO}_{2}$</tex> waveguides by thermal scanning probe lithography.

articleTitle: Hollow-Core Fiber-Based Curvature Sensor with High Sensitivity and Large Dynamic Range
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We study the application of a tubular-lattice hollow-core fiber displaying thin cladding tubes as a high-sensitivity and large-dynamic range curvature sensor. The device working principle is based on bending-induced core and cladding modes couplings occurring at specific wavelengths and at specific curvature radii. Our characterizations allowed us to determine a sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{29.3} \pm \mathbf{0.4})\ \mathbf{nm}/\mathbf{m}^{-1}$</tex> for a curvature variation range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{17}\ \mathbf{m}^{-\mathbf{1}}$</tex>. These figures are high when compared with other curvature sensors based on different optical fiber-based sensing configurations. We understand that our work provides a valid path for achieving new hollow-core curvature sensors with enhanced sensitivity and large dynamic range.

articleTitle: Mathematical Prediction of Singlet Oxygen Generation Through Sonoluminescence Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Singlet oxygen <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(^{1}O_{2})$</tex> is the primary reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated in both sono (SDT) and photodynamic (PDT) therapies. In SDT, sonoluminescence (SL) is considered the main source of ROS, though its exact role remains debated. To assess 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$o_{2}$</tex> production via SL excitation, a mathematical model was implemented, considering the overlap between the SL spectrum and the absorbance spectra of various photosensitizers. While the model slightly underestimates compared to experimental data, it is capable of predicting singlet oxygen generation resulting from SL, providing valuable insights into the process.

articleTitle: The Role of the Student Chapter in Scientific Outreach: An Experience Report in the Field of Optics and Photonics in Brazil
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This paper reviews the activities conducted by a student chapter of optics and photonics in Brazil during the 2023–2024 academic year. The initiative played a significant role within its host institution, contributing to scientific outreach and academic enrichment. The paper assesses key initiatives and their impact on both the broader community and the institution itself. We highlight several events organized during this period, which engaged over 1,500 participants. Additionally, the paper examines the benefits derived from these activities for the institutions, the participants, and the general public, emphasizing their contribution to the dissemination of optics and photonics within the community.

articleTitle: On the Complexity of Chromatic Dispersion Compensation Based on End-to-End Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In order to verify and validate the use of machine learning techniques for chromatic dispersion compensation in optical transmissions, we elaborated an end-to-end recurrent neural network aiming at replacing the conventional digital signal processing (DSP) blocks employed at the transmitter and the receiver. Moreover, in order to establish a valid comparison between the conventional DSP and the integrated neural networks, we evaluate the computational complexity of each method for the same simulation scenario. Despite presenting a good performance for the compensation of chromatic dispersion, the end-to-end technique presented a significantly greater computational complexity, limiting its potential use in practical applications.

articleTitle: FTIR Spectroscopy for Seed Specie (Brachiaria Decumbens vs Brachiaria Ruziziensis) Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The identification of Brachiaria seeds is typically performed by trained personnel through visual inspection, which can lead to misclassification and impact commercial operations. This study explores Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy as an automatic method for classifying Brachiaria decumbens and Brachiaria ruziziensis seeds. Commercial seeds were cleaned and ground before analysis. The seed powder was characterized using an Agilent Cary 630 FTIR spectrometer with an ATR accessory, covering the 4000–650 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{cm}^{-1}$</tex> range. FTIR data was preprocessed using the Modified Standard Normal Variate (MSNV) method, and seed classification was performed through Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which revealed clear clustering and separation. These results suggest that this methodology provides a robust tool for agricultural analysis.

articleTitle: All-Biodegradable Agar-Core, Agar-Cladding Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This paper reports a multimode optical fiber with core and cladding made of agar, a biodegradable and edible material. This waveguide has singular characteristics, such as reversible thermal gelation and moldability, and adjustable properties like refractive index and core/cladding diameters. Moreover, the fibers are biocompatible and present a low-cost and straightforward fabrication. We fabricate the cladding using a dip coating technique. Submerging a no-core agar fiber into melted agar-glycerol solutions with lower refractive indexes produces a surrounding layer with adjustable thickness. We characterized the optical loss through the cut-back technique, achieving 0.35 dB/cm at 632 nm. Results are comparable to other biodegradable waveguides, which suggests further applications in sensing, imaging, and illumination.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Nonlinear Distortion in Single-Channel Coherent DP-16QAM Optical Interconnects Employing Decision Tree-Based Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this study, we investigate how hyper-parameters influence the effectiveness of a nonlinear decision-tree-based classifier in a 112-Gbps dual polarization 16-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (DP-16QAM) unrepeated single-channel link. We also assess the classifier's performance when analyzing each polarization individually compared to when both polarizations are processed together. Our findings indicate that separate processing of each polarization is more advantageous at low optical power levels, while simultaneous processing of both polarizations enhances performance at medium to high power levels.

articleTitle: Estimating Capacity and SNR Loss Induced by MDG Using ANNs in Optical SDM Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We propose an ANN-based model to estimate MDG-induced capacity and SNR loss in SDM transmission using MMSE equalizer coefficients and per-mode post-filtering SNR. Simulation and experiments validate its accuracy.

articleTitle: Pump Controlled Nd:YVO4 Random Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Yttrium vanadate doped with neodymium crystal powder random laser have demonstrated promising results in 1064 nm emission when pumped at a wavelength of 806 nm. In this study, we show that by using a 585 nm pump wavelength, it is possible to achieve random lasing at both 1064 nm and 1340 nm, with the emission tunable through variations in pump intensity.

articleTitle: Performance of MIMO Visible Light Communication Under Consideration of Recommended Illumination Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This work compares illumination and communication performance of 2 × 2, 3 × 2 and 4 × 2 MIMO-OFDM VLC links. Results show that not every configuration complies with the recommended illumination levels (≥300 Ix) for operation in indoor environments.

articleTitle: Portable Sensing System Based on Optical Fiber Sensors and Smartphone for the Gait Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This work shows a portable sensing system to monitor human gait characteristics using insoles instrumented with three optical fiber macro-curvature sensors interrogated by a smartphone. The insoles can be easily adapted to shoes, providing characteristics related to the gait phases by monitoring the forefoot, midfoot, and hindfoot simultaneously. A single module containing the light source and the interrogation unit fulfills the portability requirement. The system provides spatial and temporal parameters of the gait.

articleTitle: Cost-Efficient Deep Learning Method for Mass Inverse Design of Photonic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We apply an efficient inverse design methodology to conceive metasurface-based beam deflectors. We start by creating a small dataset composed by the results of simple simulations to train two deep neural networks. Once the models are trained, various beam deflectors can be inverse designed without further full-wave simulations. Our approach combines physical intuition about blazed gratings with a state-of-the-art optimization methodology, achieving high efficiencies while requiring modest computational effort. One design was successfully fabricated using sub-20 nm thermal scanning probe lithography.

articleTitle: Harmonic Minimization Method for Pd Plasmonic Diffraction Grating Design
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The phenomenon of diffraction has been important for the development of optical technology in integrated optics, spectroscopy, and plasmonics, among others. Different mathematical formalisms have been proposed to describe the reflectance of diffraction gratings. Given that this structure is a possible experimental configuration to observe the phenomenon of Surface Plasmon Resonance, there is an engineering effort to create design algorithms that provide high-sensitivity structures for sensing and spectroscopy applications. This work proposes a design algorithm based on the Rayleigh formalism associated with a harmonic minimization method to obtain gratings with high sensitivity and rectangular profiles, with low computational effort. Multiple Pd structures are optimized for three different incident wavelengths in the infrared aiming an application in hydrogen spectral sensing devices.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Magneto-Plasmonic Hybrid Au-Fe(Oxide) Nanoparticles and Their Use as SERS Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Magneto-plasmonics (MP) refers to nanomaterials that simultaneously exhibit plasmonic and magnetic phenomena, typically achieved by combining plasmonic materials like Au, Ag, and Cu with magnetic 3d metals and their oxides. We present experimental results on the laser ablation synthesis in solution (LASiS) of Au-Fe(oxide) core-shell nanoparticles (NP) in water. Our nanoparticles were characterized through UV-Vis spectroscopy, Transmission Electron Microscopy, Dynamic Light Scattering, and Raman spectroscopy. As a proof-of-concept, we successfully used our Au-Fe(oxide) NP as substrates in Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) to detect minute amounts of biological molecules like thiourea and urea in aqueous solutions.

articleTitle: Infrared Spectroscopy Imaging of Cardiac Atria From Mice Treated with Interleukin-1beta: A Preliminary Clustering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study explores the application of Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy imaging to analyze changes in the cardiac atria of mice treated with interleukin-1 beta (IL-1beta), a cytokine known to influence cardiac remodeling. By employing k-means clustering on the spectral data, we identified distinct clusters that differentiate between IL-1beta-treated tissues and controls. The analysis revealed significant spectral differences, particularly in the amide band region, which suggests variations in protein content. These preliminary findings will be expanded into a more thorough investigation of the composition of IL-1beta-treated tissues.

articleTitle: Prototyping and Validation of Electro-Optical Transmitter for 1.2-Tb/s per Channel Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the design and prototyping of an electro-optical transceiver developed in silicon integrated photonics for operation in optical transmissions with capacity of up to 300 Gb/s per optical carrier, including the design stages of the radio frequency electrical circuits and electro-optical integration. Experimental results are presented for the validation of its transmitter employed for the generation of a wavelength-multiplexed carrier in an optical channel with an aggregate transmission rate of 1.2 Tb/s.

articleTitle: 24 mJ Single Pulse Energy from a Nd:YLF/Cr:YAG Laser in a DBMC Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This work presents a high-power Nd:YLF/Cr:YAG laser in a Double Beam Mode Controlling configuration, achieving a single pulse energy of 24 mJ, with a pulse duration of 15 ns, emitting at 1053 nm. The configuration demonstrated significant improvements in beam quality, with measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{M}^{2}$</tex> values of 2.13 vertically and 2.42 horizontally when compared to single-pass configurations. These results highlight the effectiveness of the DBMC approach in enhancing beam quality while maintaining high energy output.

articleTitle: Optimizing Gold Nanoparticles for Broadband Light Heating
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The ever-increasing demand for energy across the countries in the world imposes a constant growth in the global supply of energy to meet production and living needs. In this sense, energy production accounts for around 75% of global greenhouse gas emissions and is the largest contributor to climate change through the burning of fossil fuels and biomass. Therefore, to reduce global emissions it's crucial to shift our energy sources from fossil fuels to renewables, a challenge for developing countries that must grow their economies while providing access to good living conditions and services to its populations while reducing poverty, without relying on the extensively destructive pathways explored by developed economies in the past and present. Hereupon, the size-dependent absorption of gold nanoparticles has been explored to improve performance of Direct Absorption Solar Collectors in solar energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Migration and Alignment of Fibroblasts: Comparison between the Effects of the Polarization of Laser And A Non-Laser Device
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Although laser radiation is electromagnetic, its electric field polarization is rarely considered in photobiomodulation. This study compared the effects of laser polarization (parallel or perpendicular to the wound axis) with an electric field from a non-laser device on fibroblast migration and alignment. Human dermis fibroblasts were cultured, and a wound was inflicted. Cultures were evaluated under five conditions: parallel electric field(E//), perpendicular electric field(Epp), parallel polarized laser(L//), perpendicular polarized laser(Lpp), and control. All treatments increased cell migration compared to the control. Cells in the L// were more aligned after six hours, and those in the Epp group after 12 hours.

articleTitle: Assessment of Products Generated by Photodynamic and Sonodynamic Action Via Liquid Chromatography - Tandem Mass Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Photodynamic and sonodynamic action rely on the interaction of a sensitizing molecule with light and ultrasound, respectively, generating reactive oxygen species. These interactions also lead to the generation of other products, which might be cytotoxic or photoactive. Identifying them may help to understand the mechanisms involved in each action. So, detecting and characterizing the products become very important. This work aimed to identify the products generated by photodynamic and sonodynamic action and discuss the degradation mechanisms associated with sonodynamic action. The well-known organic sensitizers, Protoporphyrin IX, Methylene Blue, Curcumin, and Chlorin e6 were used to mediate photodynamic and sonodynamic action. Liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) was used as the detection method. The detected ions’ mass/charge ratio and retention time were summarized.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fully-Loaded Conditions in Multiband Elastic Optical Networks Using GSNR
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Multiband Elastic Optical Networks (EONs) face significant operational challenges due to the complex physical layer effects that impact transmission. Calculating the generalized signal-to-noise ratio (GSNR) of the channels is crucial for the design of these networks and the definition of operational margins. However, the variability of connections together with the existence of guard bands in EONs make imprecise the definition of a Fully-Loaded condition. This paper analysis this problem and suggests two possible simple procedures for defining a sufficient Fully-Loaded condition in EONs.

articleTitle: A Deep Neural Network Approach for Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Early detection and diagnosis of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) are essential for improving patient outcomes. This study presents the development of a deep neural network model trained to classify OSCC using hyperspectral FTIR spectroscopy imaging. The network's performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The model demonstrated high effectiveness in classifying unfolded OSCC hyperspectral images, showing potential as a valuable tool for supporting diagnostic processes in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Analysis of Signal Amplitudes in Fiber Optic Interferometric Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of interference signals generated by interferometers using the Monte Carlo method. The primary objective is to distinguish between two contributing signals within the interference pattern. The analysis is conducted in two phases: first, the numerical method is validated, and second, it is applied ex-perimentally. The results demonstrate that the Monte Carlo method effectively differentiates the signals, offering valuable insights into the characteristics of the interferometric system. The findings underscore the method's efficiency and accuracy in analyzing interference signals, making it a powerful tool for applications involving complex interference patterns.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Precision of the Transfer Matrix Method Applied to Optical Coupling Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) is widely used to efficiently simulate multi-layer optical structures. Considering the effective refractive index of guided modes, the TMM can be applied to calculate the optical coupling of Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs). This manuscript describes the analysis of the precision of a new TMM model adapted to edge coupling simulation. The results are compared with full-wave electromagnetic simulations and the similarity between the two methods is assessed. The results show that the TMM can calculate coupling reflectances as low as -40 dB with less than 2 dB of difference compared to the electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: iAnG: Species-Specific Leishmania DNA Detection via LAMP Coupled with Gold Nanorods Biosensors and Depolarized Dynamic Light Scattering
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for species-specific Leishmania molecular detection through isothermal DNA amplification (LAMP) from three species of clinical importance in Brazil (Leishmania amazonensis, L. braziliensis, and L. infantum). This approach combines photonics and nanotechnology by developing specific gold nanorods (GNrs) biosensors for each specie that we call here iAnG - isothermal DNA Amplification and Nano Gold. They were designed to interact directly with their respective LAMP amplicons, enabling short DNA amplification reactions and direct detection after just 15 minutes. This method is crucial as it offers a new rapid detection technique for a neglected tropical disease considered a global health problem. The direct detection capability addresses the major limitation of LAMP - false positives caused by nonspecific amplifications. Our work successfully developed efficient and effective sensor systems that selectively detect their targets, paving the way for future applications of gold nanorod biosensors and Depolarized Dynamic Light Scattering (DDLS) in Leishmaniasis diagnosis.

articleTitle: Decomposition Method to Speed Up Optimization Loops Containing Monte Carlo Simulations to Estimate Radioisotope Production
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Monte Carlo simulations are an essential tool for modeling radioisotope production through nuclear reactions. However, they can be computationally demanding, especially when running optimization loops that require many simulations. This study addresses this limitation by demonstrating a decrease in computation time over 5 orders of magnitude by decomposing an electron energy spectrum into an orthogonal basis that was Monte Carlo pre-propagated, to estimate radioisotope production from bremsstrahlung induced photo-nuclear reactions. A comparative analysis of fifty electron spectra showed that this method could replicate the results of original spectra simulations with minimal discrepancies, with errors typically below 8%.

articleTitle: Lead-Acid Battery Electrolyte Density Sensor using Heterocore Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) have gained popularity due to the importance of energy self-sufficiency for some systems. In this context, significant investments have been made in research to enhance the reliability of BESS operations. Addressing these reliability concerns, this work proposes using a refractometer based on a heterocore optical fiber to monitor electrolyte concentrations in real-time. This monitoring can be used to evaluate the battery health and optimize maintenance management. The sensor was fabricated using a 30.7 mm long no-core optical fiber between two multimode optical fibers, achieving a sensitivity of 0.0153 dB/(g/L).

articleTitle: Demonstration of ϕ-OTDR-Based DFOS Assisted by YOLOv8 for Traffic Monitoring in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We investigate the viability of using legacy fiber infrastructure to support future smart cities using distributed fiber optic sensing (DFOS) for traffic control. We carry out a field trial using fibers installed along the university campus and a dedicated camera for traffic parameter estimation. The novel YOLOv8 pattern recognition model applied to recorded video sequences is used as a reference to validate the implemented phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometer (ϕ-OTDR). The collected ϕ-OTDR data is manually annotated and compared to the YOLOv8 data used as ground truth. The results indicate that the implemented ϕ-OTDR setup successfully detects heavy vehicle traffic.

articleTitle: Galvanometer-Based 2D Optical Scanner: Trajectory Modeling and Linearization
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss optical scanning systems based on galvanometers. Such systems, widely used both in image projection and signal reading, present undesirable characteristics of signal deformation. The main idea of this work is to determine an analytical mathematical model for the scan and, consequently, its deformations and propose the implementation of corrections for these deformations in an analytical way. At the end, comparisons of scan results with and without the implemented corrections are presented.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Nonlinear Polarization in a High-Power YDCFL
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Avstract- This work investigates the influence of temperature, pump power, and upper-level population density on the nonlinear refractive index of a high-power Yb-doped double-cladding fiber laser (YDCFL) operating in the CW regime, in the forward pumping configuration. A theoretical model that examines how these physical variables impact the nonlinear polarization of a ytterbium-doped optical fiber is presented. This phenomenon can result in nonlinear effects in the YDCFL.

articleTitle: FTIR Spectroscopy of Biofluids for Disease Diagnosis: Data Quality Influence on Group Separation
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) Spectroscopy, particularly using the Attenuated Total Reflection (ATR) technique, has become a powerful tool in the analysis of biofluids for diagnostic purposes. The effectiveness of this technique in disease diagnosis relies heavily on the quality of the acquired spectral data. This study investigates the impact of key experimental parameters, such as the number of scans and spectral resolution, on the quality of FTIR spectra. By analyzing blood serum samples from different groups, we explore how these parameters influence the performance of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers in clustering tasks. Our findings indicate that while higher resolution does not necessarily enhance clustering, an increased number of scans can significantly improve classification performance when combined with lower-resolution settings. This work underscores the importance of optimizing FTIR data acquisition parameters to build robust predictive models in clinical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Response to the Treatment of Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer Using Photodynamic Therapy in Diabetic Mice
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Cancer treatment will continue to be a global health challenge and photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a light-based, non-invasive technique in the treatment of non-melanoma skin cancer. However, the elderly usually have other comorbidities such as diabetes and how they interact with ALA-PDT in the treatment of skin cancer is still unknown. We established a diabetic and tumorigenic model in Balb/c nude mice with A431 cells and investigated the effects of PDT compared to non-diabetic mice. Preliminary results showed a delay in tumor formation accompanied by harsher weight loss. Future analyses in respirometry could reveal differences in mitochondrial energy production.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Nonlinear Refractive Index in a High-Power YDCFL Using the RK4 Method
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This work presents an analysis of the variation of the nonlinear refractive index in a high-power Yb-doped double-cladding fiber laser (YDCFL) induced by the pump power. The RK4 numerical method was employed to solve the ordinary differential equation describing the behavior of the pump power in the YDCFL operating in a continuous wave (CW) forward configuration. As a result, the nonlinear refractive index behavior along the longitudinal direction of the optical fiber was obtained.

articleTitle: Contributions to the Design of Laser Wakefield Acceleration >30 MeV at High Repetition Rates with Parameters Obtained by Particle-in-Cell Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Relativistic electron beams can be produced by laser wakefield acceleration (LWFA) and the generation of quasimonoenergetic electrons at high repetition rates with energies of the order of 100 MeV are required for important applications. This work reviews and summarizes some simulation results of these accelerators that we have recently performed and their correlation with new experimental results that implement and demonstrate the predicted results. Some proposals for new designs are also presented.

articleTitle: Evidence a Phonon Laser Triggered by Photon Avalanche in Nd3+ Ions
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In recent years, the photon avalanche (PA) phenomenon has attracted great interest from the scientific community, especially with the use of rare earth ions doped in different matrices. This phenomenon, discovered 45 years ago, involves dipole-dipole interactions, such as cross-relaxations, allowing a detailed study of PA in Nd³⁺ ions when excited above the power threshold. Although PA is well characterized, high-power regions remained unexplored due to the monotonous dynamics of the emissions. In this research, by exploring higher powers, a new phenomenon was observed, characterized by a second power threshold, spectral broadening, and particle sintering, causing a suppression in luminescence. This behavior can be explained to stimulated phonon emission associated with the ⁴I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11/2</inf> → ⁴I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9/2</inf> transition, expanding our understanding of emissions in Nd³⁺-doped systems.

articleTitle: ATR-FTIR Spectroscopy in the Detection of Amoxicillin
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)

authors.preferredName: Caroline Guimarães Pançardes da Silva Marangoni

abstract: Amoxicillin is still one of the most common antibiotics to treat bacterial infections. Although conventional drug monitoring techniques often exhibit significant limitations in terms of accuracy and analysis speed, optical-based methods can be introduced as an appealing option for this purpose. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) has been long established and implemented across various fields, including biomedical, clinical, and pharmaceutical. This work presents an alternative approach to the usual amoxicillin detection and monitoring procedures using vibrational spectroscopy. In this preliminary investigation, our results show several characteristics for quantification, with limit of detection of 93 µM, point to the high potential of the technique for drug monitoring.

articleTitle: Rapid Identification of Breast Cancer in Different Stages Using Micro-FTIR and Supervised Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the second most common cancer in the world; 11.5% of the total cases of cancer in both genders and 15.4% of deaths in females are reported. Accurate determination of the intrinsic subtype and disease stage of breast cancer will help in the adoption of optimal treatment strategies, thus improving overall outcomes. The aim of the present work, therefore, is to apply micro-FTIR spectroscopy combined with different supervised machine learning methods to classify various types and stages of breast cancer and to identify the chemometric areas that best distinguish between them. In the work reported here, PCA-LDA and PLS-DA models were carried out in the raw data in the fingerprint region (1800–900 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$cm^{-1})$</tex> and the region characteristic for proteins (1750–1400 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$cm^{-1})$</tex>. Therefore, the analysis of these results reveals significant differences in the amide I and amide II regions, thus proving that both PCA-LDA and PLS-DA are useful frameworks for performing discrimination analyses.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Grating Sensor Design for Pressure Detection in Compressed Air Pipeline System
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Compressed air systems are central to modern industrial production, and leakage is one of the most significant sources of energy losses, wasting energy and reducing equipment efficiency. The proposed work involves designing and developing a diaphragm FBG pressure sensor using EVA as a membrane for compressed air system monitoring. The sensor measures pressures in the range of 0 kPa to 400 kPa, the sensitivity obtained was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$((12.9\pm 0.4)\text{pm}/\text{kPa})$</tex>, with a linearity of 0.14 nm and a resolution of 0.7 kPa when the pressure decreases from 400 kPa to 0 kPa.

articleTitle: Second Harmonic Generation in Bulk ReS2 with Hybrid AA-AB Stacking
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We report the optical second harmonic generation of mechanically exfoliated bulk ReS2 with hybrid AA-AB stacking. The results showed a high nonlinear signal 45 times stronger than monolayer MOS2.

articleTitle: Polymethyl Methacrylate-based Light Collector for Enhanced Indoor Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: A new polymethyl methacrylate-based light collector has been designed and fabricated with additive manufacturing to optimize the efficiency of VLC systems. It enhances the area of detection, leading to a ~ 1.9x increase in power performance and low BER values in the VLC link.

articleTitle: Spatial Effects of Second Harmonic Generation with Non-Diffracting Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We studied the second harmonic generation with non-diffracting beams. We provided analytical calculations that explains observed experimental and numerical results, demonstrating that when all the plane waves composing the non-diffracting fields are in phase-match with the crystal, in the thin crystal approximation, the effect is to obtain the square of the incident field in the second harmonic generation. As an application it can be used to spatially clean speckle fields.

articleTitle: Flat Optical Frequency Comb Generation Using Woodward's Theorem
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This paper presents a mathematical model and the associated setup to generate flat optical frequency combs based on Woodward's Theorem and frequency modulation (FM). The simulation results confirm the proposed optical system.

articleTitle: Investigating Photosensitizing Properties of Methylene Blue on Perfusate Solutions Decontamination for Organ Preservation
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this study, methylene blue (MB) was evaluated as a photosensitizer for photodynamic therapy aimed for decontaminating organ perfusates used during transplantation. The absorption spectroscopy and liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC-MS) were employed to follow up the MB photodegradation. The in vitro antimicrobial efficacy of photodynamic therapy was investigated through microbiological assays using Staphylococcus aureus. The findings suggest the interaction of MB with biomolecules present in perfusates significantly attenuate its photodynamic activity, potentially by trapping its molecules and thereby diminishing its interaction with bacterial cells.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based PAM-4 Optical Modulator on Side-Polished Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Recently, graphene has emerged as a promising material for optical modulators due to its small size, low energy consumption, and high modulation depth. In our research, we design a capacitive structure on a side-polished optical fiber that can modulate light into four different signal levels, resulting in a Pulse Amplitude Modulation 4-level (PAM-4) format. Our methods for designing and producing the multilevel modulator structure enable us to achieve a cutoff frequency of 229 MHz (458 Mbps) and a drive voltage of 4.77 V.

articleTitle: Enhancing and Evaluating Edge-Coupling Between Fiber Microlenses and Integrated Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This work presents a method for enhancing and evaluating optical edge-coupling employing microlenses in photonic integrated circuits (PICs) by monitoring the reflected signal of the Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) formed between the elements. By measuring the free spectral range (FSR) of the FPI, it is possible to evaluate key parameters, such as the length and refractive index of the coupling region. When combined with an iterative positioning scheme, this method can be applied to automate and improve the alignment process between a microlens and an integrated waveguide.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Modal Dispersion in Graded-Index Multimode Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this paper, we compare the modal dispersion (MD) in standard and bend-insensitive graded-index multimode fibers (GI-MMFs and BI-MMFs). By selectively exciting 45 modes across 9 mode groups, we observed a maximum differential group delay (between mode group 9 and mode group 1) of 1.14 ns/km in BI-MMF and 2.02 ns/km in standard MMF. The reduced modal dispersion in BI-MMFs is attributed to their trench-structured index profile. Additionally, we discuss the effects of mode coupling on signal integrity and the complexities it introduces for equalization in multimode optical systems.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Imaging System in a Spectrometer for Laser Accelerated Electrons
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We present here the development of an imaging system for an electron spectrometer aiming at the characterization of laser-accelerated electrons. The spectrometer features a constant magnetic field that deflects electrons, based on their kinetic energy, which hit a scintillator that luminesces; an imaging system captures this luminescence and projects it onto a digital camera outside a vacuum chamber. The imaging system is designed to optimize the collection of the luminescence and to produce a demagnified image on the digital camera. A theoretical and experimental analysis of the lenses foci and positioning is presented, resulting in a final assemblage.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Mitigation of Nonlinear Intersymbol Interference in Digital Coherent Optical Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This paper explores the interaction between dispersion-induced intersymbol interference and self-phase modulation in coherent optical communication systems using raised cosine pulse shaping. In order to address this interaction, we trained a multilayer perceptron with adjacent symbols, demonstrating that utilizing information from multiple symbols enhances the system's ability to compensate for nonlinear distortion.

articleTitle: Broadband Tunable Metal-Dielectric Color Filters for the Visible Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The use of adjustable filters has increased considerably in recent years. In this work, we present the concept and design of an ultra-fine, electrically tunable transmission mode color filter, whose transmission mode spectrum is electrically tunable in the visible spectrum region. A simple Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) cavity configuration is used, with electro-optical dielectric material 4-dimethylamino-N-methyl-4-stilbazolium-tosylate (DAST) as a dielectric layer and silver as the metal layers. By varying the applied voltage from -6V to +6V, the filter's transmission spectrum is dynamically tuned across the visible range from 425nm to 641nm with transmission values from 0.63 to 0.75, enabling continuous color adjustment from violet to red. This tunability is achieved without the need of complex lithography, making the filter suitable for applications in optical switching, smart windows, and light-emitting devices. The results demonstrate that the proposed design offers broad tunability with potential for integration into various photonic systems.

articleTitle: Antimicrobial Effect of Reactive Iodine Species Produced by Photodynamic Therapy Against Streptococcus Pneumoniae in a Lung Alveolar Transwell Model
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) effectiveness against pathogenic microorganisms can be enhanced by potassium iodide (KI). KI achieves this by forming longer-lived reactive iodine species (RIS), compared to the reactive oxygen species (ROS) in conventional PDT. This study investigated the synergistic effects of KI and Methylene Blue (MB) in aPDT against Streptococcus pneumoniae within a lung alveolar transwell model. Results showed that KI significantly enhanced MB-mediated aPDT, increasing efficacy against S. pneumoniae colony-forming units (CFUs). Notably, the photoproducts (RIS) alone reduced S. pneumoniae CFUs by over 3 logs without harming mammalian cells. This highlights the potential of KI-enhanced aPDT.

articleTitle: Study of Antimicrobial Efficacy of Photodynamic Therapy in Candida Albicans Culture Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Photodynamic Therapy associates photosensitizing agents associated with a light source. This association produces Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS). These ROS have antimicrobial action against certain pathogens. Objective: To determine the minimum inhibitory concentration of the photosensitizers Orthotoluidine Blue and Methylene Blue when sensitized by the light-emitting diode in Candida albicans culture. Methodology: We performed an in vitro study of different doses of LED exposure and different concentrations of the photosensitizers, aiming at the inactivation of the fungus C. albicans. The LED equipment was a cluster power of 0.15 W with a wavelength of 630 nm. The experiment used three dosages of photodynamic therapy: LED for 15 seconds (5.92 J/cm2), LED for 30 seconds (11.84 J/cm2) and the same light dosages with an increase in the number of subgroups evaluating the efficacy of photodynamic therapy. Results: The minimum concentration of toluidine blue was found in the last two phases with a concentration of 0.7μM. Methylene blue PS did not show favorable effects. Conclusion: This study demonstrated that methylene blue is not a good choice for use in photodynamic therapy aiming at antimicrobial effects against Candida Albicans using a light source with a cluster power of 0.15 W and a wavelength of 630 nm. In another aspect, toluidine blue showed a minimum concentration of 0.7μM in Candida Albicans cultures using a light source with a cluster power of 0.15 W and a wavelength of 630 nm.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of a High-Power YDCFL Operating in Forward and Two-end Pumping Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This study compares high-power Yb-doped double-cladding fiber lasers (YDCFLs) operating in forward and two-end pumping configurations. The temperature profile, changes in the nonlinear refractive index, thermal power density, and nonlinear polarization were analyzed under these pumping conditions. The results indicate that the bidirectional configuration provides superior thermal stability, while the unidirectional configuration is more susceptible to nonlinear effects.

articleTitle: Effective Luminescent Sensor Element for Monitoring Dissolved Oxygen
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The precipitation of expanded polystyrene (EPS) waste aggregated with platinum octaethylporphyrin (PtOEP) was synthesized to fabricate and characterize an effective oxygen-sensitive thin film sensor element. The synthesized polymer-sensitive layer presents a linear Stern-Volmer (SV) quenching relation to probe dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration. The luminescence quenching (LQ) of the fabricated element shows similar figures of merit as compared to a commercial DO sensor cap measured under the same experimental conditions.

articleTitle: Development of a Fiber Optic Inertial Measurement Unit for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In this work, we present the development of a fiber optic inertial measurement unit (IMU), for space application. The IMU comprises three orthogonal closed-loop interferometric fiber optic gyroscopes (IFOGs) and a triaxial fiber optic accelerometer (TRACC), for determination of attitude and heading in 3D-space. The IFOG developed reached a bias drift of 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times{1}0^{-3}{}^\circ/\mathrm{h}$</tex> and angular random walk of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.9 \times 10^{-4}\circ/\sqrt{\mathrm{h}}$</tex>, while the TRACC presented bias drift of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.6 \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{g}$</tex> and velocity random walk of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.8 \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}/\sqrt{\mathrm{h}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Antibiotic Monitoring Employing Raman/SERS Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)

authors.preferredName: Caroline Guimarães Pançardes Da Silva Marangoni

abstract: Rapid and accurate detection of antibiotics is a critical challenge in the healthcare field, but a new approach based on Raman/SERS spectroscopy could be a solution. This research uses this technique to present the acquisition of spectra (“fingerprints”) of vancomycin, little explored in the scientific literature, and ciprofloxacin antibiotics. The analyses allowed understanding how the nanoparticles (Au, Ag and Cu) can influence the SERS spectrum acquisition of each antibiotic. The results showed that the Raman spectroscopy technique can provide unique spectra for each type of antibiotic evaluated, allowing for their precise identification.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Increasing Beam Quality by Adapting Mode Field Radius at Pump-signal Combiner's Signal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: High transmission efficiency, low insertion loss, and high beam quality are interesting characteristics of beam combiners. These devices have enabled power coupling in the fiber laser's active medium, and their performance has a strong impact on the fiber laser's efficiency. In this paper, the increase in the optical beam quality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^{2}$</tex> was analyzed by adapting the modal radius of the combiner signal fiber. The formulation is supported by the Finite Difference Beam Propagation Method (FD-BPM) and Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT), and they were implemented in Matlab.

articleTitle: Ultra-Efficient Modulators Based on Chalcogenide and Graphene Materials for AI Hyperscalers
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Driven by the global growth in AI services, the demand for efficient hardware is at an all-time high in the race for continued performance scaling of hyperscale data centers. Integrated photonics devices have emerged as a promising alternative for reducing energy consumption. We report an optical modulator design that incorporates chalcogenide and graphene materials to achieve the minimal power consumption per bit during high-speed operation. The device design and its energy consumption performance are presented. Our results pave the way for ultra-efficient modulators revealing operations at high-speed modulation bandwidth up to 104 GHz whilst reducing energy consumption to 52.3 fJ/bit.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of SP Microcavities Before and After the Thermal Oxidation Process
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: In the present, we investigate the optical properties of porous silicon (Psi) microcavities fabricated from N-type silicon. Using optical characterization techniques, we analyze the influence of thermal oxidation processes on the resonant properties of the microcavities. The Psi microcavities were fabricated through controlled electrochemical anodization, resulting in one-dimensional photonic crystals with tunable band gaps. We observed that precise control of the oxidation process allows fine-tuning of the optical properties of the microcavities, which is crucial for applications in high-sensitivity optical sensors and optoelectronic devices. The results show a strong correlation between the nanometric structure of Psi and the efficiency of optical confinement, highlighting the potential of N-type porous silicon for the development of advanced photonic technologies opening new possibilities for the enhancement of devices based on photonic crystals.

articleTitle: Hybrid Training for 5G Linearization Systems Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Radio over Fiber systems blend the efficiency of fiber optic transmission with the flexibility of wireless communications but face significant challenges due to inherent nonlinearities in optical signal transmission. This paper proposes a hybrid training technique using simulated and real data to train machine learning models deployed for linearization, aiming to enhance performance and reliability. The proposal involves pre-training the model with a large synthetic dataset and fine-tuning it with real data collected from experiments. This method leverages synthetic data to establish initial weights, refined using real-world data to capture practical complexities. Results show that the hybrid training technique significantly outperforms models trained solely on synthetic data, with nearly a twofold improvement in performance as evidenced by lower Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values. Compared to models trained exclusively on real data, the hybrid method achieves comparable performance, proving effective in scenarios where real data is scarce or hard to obtain.

articleTitle: State-of-the-Art Neural Network-Based Equalizers for Coherent Optical Communication Systems: Architectures and Complexity
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: This paper reviews recent advancements in neural network (NN)-based equalizers for coherent optical communication systems, with a focus on their architecture and complexity. Various approaches are surveyed across transmission schemes, including single-channel, wavelength-division multiplexing, and digital subcarrier multiplexing systems. The study highlights the effectiveness of NNs in mitigating nonlinear impairments, improving signal quality, and transmission capacity. An overview of reduced-complexity NN-based equalizers in different transmission schemes is also provided, demonstrating their potential for real-time applications in future high-speed optical networks.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Localized Surface Plasmon-Er3+ Coupling in the Near-Infrared Emission at Low Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: The coupling between rare-earth ions and localized surface plasmons has been recently investigated, especially under controlled temperature. This research explores the quantum-plasmonic behavior in Au nanoparticles embedded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Er}^{3+}$</tex> -tellurite glasses. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Er}^{3+}$</tex> emission at 1536 nm is analyzed, and a significant enhancement of the FWHM and the emission intensities are obtained. Such enhancements result from the improvement of the localized surface plasmon and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Er}^{3+}$</tex> coupling since, under cooling conditions, the plasmon modes expand, increasing the local field enhancement.

articleTitle: Optical Power Injection Approaches in Photonic Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Silicon photonics is a predominant and revolutionary platform in integrated photonics that enables the realization of a multitude of components and systems that cover several applications related to computing, communication, and sensing. Regardless of the device/system that can be implemented through this platform, an issue of academic and industrial interest lies in the injection of optical power/signal into Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs). This manuscript provides a brief review of some approaches used to power the PIC. First, we will address the issues and solutions related to the coupling of a signal from a laser to a PIC. Finally, we will address the approaches for heterogeneous integration between the light source and the PIC, where III-V-on-silicon technologies will be highlighted.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Topological Features on Ordering Routing and Spectrum Assignment in Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: We explore the influence of topological features on a hybrid routing and spectrum assignment (HRSA) algorithm in elastic optical networks that prioritizes either routing or spectrum assignment for network source-destination node pairs. We use logistic regression to extract information about how the HRSA makes its decision, whether it is about prioritizing proper routing or spectrum assignment choices based on efficient solutions returned by the HRSA. Results show that the proposed model achieved 81% of accuracy and provided insights on how topological features impact the decision-making criteria of HRSA.

articleTitle: From Coherent Communications to Quantum Security: Modern Techniques in CV-QKD
publicationTitle: 2024 SBFoton International Optics and Photonics Conference (SBFoton IOPC)
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) leverages quantum information theory to enable two remote parties to establish a random key with unconditional secrecy. Performing QKD with coherent light states integrates with modern optical communication techniques but presents new challenges. This survey reviews advancements in applying digital signal processing (DSP) techniques, transformative in coherent optical communications, to continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD). We discuss how DSP methods enhance CV-QKD performance, security, and feasibility. The areas examined include phase estimation, channel equalization, error correction, and noise reduction, highlighting associated challenges and future research directions.
